newsitem.title: CANADA: Cargill Foods expands Canadian beef plant.
newsitem.headline: Cargill Foods expands Canadian beef plant.

text.p: Cargill Foods said it has begun a full second shift operation at its High River, Alberta beef processing plant.

The facility, which was recently expanded at a cost of C$37 million, is now capable of processing 3,500 head of cattle per day. The capacity prior to expansion was around 2,000 head, a spokeswoman told Reuters.

The company said the development of a second shift started in January but it only reached its full capacity during the last month. Cargill Foods is a division of Cargill Ltd, the Canadian subsidiary of Cargill Inc.
Cargill Ltd president Kerry Hawkins said in a release that much of the second shift production was destined for the international marketplace.
"For several years now, the agricultural industry has recognized that there is far more economic value in exporting processed rather than raw products," said Hawkins.
The fully integrated facility houses slaughter, fabrication, rendering and hide operations, the company said.
